      The commutative square with a Frobenius conjugate yields an equivariant differential for the resulting semilinear maps.

      theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.FieldExtension.semilinearEquiv_coefficientMap {k F R : Type u} [Field k] [Field F] [Algebra k F] [Ring R] [Algebra k R] [Module.Finite k R] {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L] (e : F →ₐ[k] L) (σ : Gal(F/k)) (τ : Gal(L/k)) (h : ∀ (c : F), e (σ c) = τ (e c)) {X : ScalarCategory k F (FGModuleCat R)} (a : X ≅ X) (x : ↑(extendObj k F R X.obj)) :
      let G := extendScalarCategory k F R; let H := extendScalarCategory k L R; let J := ScalarCategory.changeScalars e; (semilinearEquiv τ (H.mapIso (J.mapIso a))) ((coefficientMap e X.obj) x) = (coefficientMap e X.obj) ((semilinearEquiv σ (G.mapIso a)) x)

      The semilinear maps on two successive extensions agree on vectors over the smaller extension when their field automorphisms agree there.
